name: Claymation
visualIdentity: Matte clay, subtle fingerprints, credible contact, and volume-preserving poses that change in discrete exposures under stable light. Authentic clay is photographed; a digital clay-like look must be identified as a simulation. Avoid unrestricted liquid flow and glossy plastic reflections.
suitableUses: Playful character shorts, crafted product or explainer scenes, and miniature narratives. This supplemental reference is not claimed as a directly named source-collection style. Suitable for video or interactive HTML when its materials and movement can be represented faithfully.
limitations: No renderer is prescribed for clay itself. Photographed clay frames or a clearly labeled Blender simulation are the stated routes. A simulated appearance does not prove physical production or validated physics. Preserve pose exposure and holds; do not automatically interpolate poses. Motion patterns require fitting assets and geometry, such as facial layers for gaze or depth layers for parallax.
palette: No canonical palette is specified. The optional matte natural-clay example uses background #F0E4D3, foreground #444B3D, and accents #A2A680 and #C58D74. Exact task, brand, or reference colors override it; preserve material colors and roles. Gradients are disabled. The accents are decorative, not suitable for normal text on their own; check contrast in the final composite.
motionAndInteraction: Use incremental pose changes, volume-preserving forms, credible contact, and readable holds. For video, derive states from seekable composition time; delivery frame rate may exceed pose exposure rate. Interactive HTML may add bounded pointer responses, scroll-linked stories or transitions, with reversible state, keyboard/touch access where relevant, and reduced-motion support. Use motion patterns only when scene assets support them; keep one owner per animated property.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience, honoring supplied audio requirements. Synchronize to the same timeline; preserve speech clarity and inspect the final mix for balance, clipping, and sync.
assetRequirements: Authentic work needs photographed, incrementally adjusted clay. Prepare transparent, consistently sized, clearly named layers or numbered frames. Digital simulation may use clay materials and discrete exposures in Blender. Preserve crop margins, contact, occlusion, and stable lighting. Audio assets must be supplied or otherwise authorized.
combinations: Expressive reaction captions can support vertical social clips if they use restrained palette accents, follow pose cadence, and avoid faces; avoid glossy effects and constant captions. Beat-table timing can align pose changes to music, while retaining weight-bearing holds and not changing every element on every beat.
productionApproach: Select visual construction and motion methods for the style, action, assets, and fidelity first; state each tool’s responsibility. Use HyperFrames by default for composition, seekable timing, synchronization, validation, and export. Remotion is only a documented fallback if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability. Python may preprocess assets; FFmpeg may encode sequences and combine audio. Drive visuals deterministically from shared time, inspect representative frames and the decoded video, and verify dimensions, frame rate, duration, sync, and loop continuity.
